Axial skeletal dysplasia; progressive retinal dystrophy and visual loss occur in 80-99%, with rod-cone dystrophy reported in 20/21.
Defined by hypertension in the portal venous circulation; common intrinsic hepatic injury is not established for this umbrella.
Spastic neurodegeneration and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome; cataracts and hypogonadism each occur in 30-79%.
Congenital hair loss and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis are disorders of hair and skin.
Congenital central hypothyroidism defines the disease; constipation and concentration difficulties do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited marrow failure and characteristic radial-ulnar and thumb malformations define the syndrome; possible lymphoma is not a universal mechanism.
A localized breast neoplasm; breast has no axis. Nerve-sheath histogenesis does not establish damage to the nervous system.
Severe developmental impairment, epilepsy and motor dysfunction define the disorder; isolated contractures and dysmorphic features do not establish common skeletal damage.
Myeloid neoplasia directly affects marrow and blood-cell production; cytopenia-related infections do not establish a separate immune disease.

Developmental impairment and epilepsy define the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in only 5-29%.

Progressive cerebellar degeneration, epilepsy and neuropathy affect the nervous system; abnormal eye movements are neurologic signs.
Dyserythropoietic anemia with an intrinsic glycosylation disorder; gallstones are separate complications, and iron deposition alone does not prove common hepatic dysfunction.
Autoimmune inflammation of scalp hair follicles causes complete scalp hair loss; associated diabetes and bowel disease are separate minority conditions.
Neonatal cholestasis and severe chronic lymphedema affecting subcutaneous tissue define the syndrome; cirrhosis occurs in ~25%; secondary nutritional complications vary.
Ependymal neoplasm arising within the central nervous system.
Redundant conjunctival folds constitute a structural disorder of the ocular surface.
Malignant bone-forming neoplasm arising on the bone surface.
Degeneration of vertebrae, intervertebral discs and supporting tissues; radiculopathy or myelopathy are separately diagnosed complications.
Bowed long-bone dysplasia and autonomic nervous-system dysfunction define the syndrome; common lasting pulmonary or ocular injury is not established across subtypes.
Benign epithelial neoplasm occupying lung tissue.
Neoplasm defined by its skull-base location; neural, sinus and endocrine involvement depend on the particular subtype.
Ataxia, sensorineural deafness and cardiomyopathy define the syndrome; unspecified skin abnormalities lack evidence of common direct damage.
